papers.title: Evaluation of hydrophilicity and surface morphology of nanosecond-pulsed laser-engineered surface textures on stainless steel, cobalt-chromium, and titanium alloys
papers.abstract: The need to improve biocompatibility and to ensure successful integration of biologically compatible metals or bio-metals with biological tissues has resulted in the development and creation of engineered surfaces as biomaterials for use as implants and bio-medical devices. Through laser surface texturing, precise control over surface micro-topography, and microstructure pattern can be achieved, that optimize and enhance cellular adhesion, growth and differentiation—key factors that prevent implant rejection and improve device functionality and performance. This study investigates nanosecond-pulsed, laser-engineered surface texturing on stainless steel, titanium, and cobalt-chromium alloys, particularly for use in biocompatible implants. Coupons of each material were textured using uniform laser parameters, resulting in engineered surfaces with distinct and defined peaks and valleys, creating micro-topographies influenced by the Gaussian profile of the laser, as analyzed via SEM (scanning electron microscopy) and optical profilometry. Surface analysis showed that engineered textures on stainless steel demonstrate high uniformity with surface roughness measured to be 0.897 μm (Ra), facilitating better cellular adhesion, an essential feature for implant integration. This was confirmed via water contact angle test that showed a moderately hydrophilic surface showing consistent behavior (mean Water Contact Angle (WCA)) close to 71.1°, variance 0.17). Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) indicated minimal surface oxidation across all samples, consistent with processing under an inert gas environment. Additionally, a computational model was created to verify and validate the “experimental surface-textured” profiles of each of the materials within a 5% margin, confirming the accuracy and reproducibility of the laser-processing technique. The uniform micro-scale surface topography and preserved surface chemistry of SS316L show that it promotes cell-adhesion and enhanced potential for biomedical implant applications compared to Co-Cr and Ti-6Al-4V.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究激光表面织构对Ti-6Al-4V等合金亲水性和表面形貌的影响，未涉及力学性能或疲劳行为，且非增材制造工艺。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on surface hydrophilicity and morphology of laser-textured Ti-6Al-4V, not on mechanical or fatigue properties, and does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF/SLM/EBM/DED).

summary_zh.motivation: 改善生物金属植入物的生物相容性
summary_zh.method: 纳秒脉冲激光表面织构化处理不锈钢、钴铬和钛合金
summary_zh.result: 不锈钢表面均匀性最好，亲水性适中，钛合金表面氧化最少
summary_zh.validation: 通过接触角测试和计算模型验证表面形貌

summary_en.motivation: To enhance biocompatibility of metallic implants through controlled surface micro-topography.
summary_en.method: Nanosecond-pulsed laser surface texturing was applied to stainless steel, cobalt-chromium, and titanium alloys with uniform parameters.
summary_en.result: Stainless steel showed highest surface uniformity and moderate hydrophilicity, while titanium alloys exhibited minimal oxidation.
summary_en.validation: Experimental water contact angle measurements and computational models confirmed surface texture accuracy within 5% margin.

papers.title: Investigation of Femur Head Implant Wear and Fatigue Properties for Climbing Upstairs and Climbing Downstairs Without Rail Support
papers.abstract: The existence of a femur implant in hip hemiarthroplasty depends on the novelty of the material used. Wear and fatigue analysis of the implant is very important to determine the life of the implant. This study comprehends molding and femur head analysis using finite element analysis, which is applied in hip replacement. Carbon-fiber-reinforced polyether ether ketone and titanium alloy with polyether ether ketone are among the materials employed for the analysis. Wear and fatigue behaviour of human interference under dynamic loading, such as climbing upstairs without rail support and climbing down stairs without rail support, is considered. SolidWorks 2021 was used for modeling, and ANSYS Workbench 19.2 was deployed for FEA. The wear depth was taken into consideration using the modified Archard's equation. The CFR PEEK has a mean stress of 10.1065 MPa during upstair and 12.3054 MPa during downstair, whereas the fatigue life of Ti-6Al-4V during upstair is 9 years and 6.756593 years during downstair. It has been calculated using the S-N curves. Equivalent stress, sliding distance, and contact pressure were the results of the FEA for every material and activity. The CFR PEEK type is the best material for the top of the femur in several actions, corresponding to the results, as well as the downstairs activity, which produced the highest stresses along with contact pressures. For proper operation, the CFR PEEK material femur head must be replaced or altered after its estimated ten-year lifespan.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究股骨头植入物在上下楼梯时的磨损和疲劳，虽然使用了Ti-6Al-4V材料，但未涉及增材制造工艺，且主要关注植入物结构，与方向L1不符。
llm.why_not_core: No additive manufacturing process; the paper focuses on implant design and wear/fatigue of a conventional Ti-6Al-4V femoral head, not on characterization of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V mechanical/fatigue properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究股骨头植入物在上下楼梯时材料磨损和疲劳寿命，以评估其使用寿命。
summary_zh.method: 使用SolidWorks和ANSYS进行有限元分析，采用修正Archard磨损方程和S-N曲线计算。
summary_zh.result: CFRPEEK磨损性能优于Ti-6Al-4V，但Ti-6Al-4V疲劳寿命约为9年。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，仅基于有限元仿真。

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to evaluate the wear and fatigue life of femur head implant materials under dynamic stair-climbing loads.
summary_en.method: Finite element analysis in ANSYS Workbench combined with modified Archard's wear equation and S-N curves.
summary_en.result: CFR-PEEK showed lower stresses, while Ti-6Al-4V exhibited a fatigue life of approximately 9 years for upstairs climbing.
summary_en.validation: Only computational simulation without experimental validation.
